items.title: Orchestrator scope and page-local ownership boundary
items.statement: Orchestrator owns scheduling, concerns, blocked-state handling, runtime identity, page layout and controls, projections, and run-control intents, but it is not itself the UI/CLI/provider and does not own canonical runtime enums, event semantics, scheduler truth, or storage truth.

evidence.exact_quote: Orchestrator is the core scheduling, concern tracking, blocked-state handling, and runtime-identity management system. It is not the UI, CLI, or external provider.

Orchestrator ownership is limited to page layout and controls, view-model/projections, and run control intents; canonical runtime enums, event semantics, and scheduler truth remain owned by runtime, storage, and scheduler contracts instead of page-local prose.

items.title: Canonical seven-tab shell and legacy alias behavior
items.statement: The page is a single-page shell with exactly seven named canonical tabs; Plan Compile is a dedicated projection and tier-era tab labels are compatibility/search aliases, not current runtime authority.

evidence.exact_quote: The /page-shell is a seven-tab single-page surface with canonical tabs `Progress`, `Plan Compile`, `Seams`, `Node Graph`, `Evidence`, `History`, and `Ledger`. Node Graph Display remains a native Orchestrator view over `Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md`, `Plans/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md`, `/Orchestrator_Page.md`, and `/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md`; `Plan Compile` is a dedicated compile projection tab, and `Tiers` plus tier-era tab labels survive only as compatibility/search aliases while the canonical runtime model is node/package/seam/lane aware.

items.title: Plan Compile launch consumes one approval transaction
items.statement: A successful Planning Wizard Approve And Build command opens Plan Compile against either a durable run id or an idempotency-keyed pending projection, then reconciles to the durable run without creating a second launch.

evidence.exact_quote: Orchestrator Plan Compile consumes the Planning Wizard `Approve And Build` approval transaction; it does not create a second ordinary build launch. When `cmd.planning_wizard.approve_and_build` succeeds locally, Orchestrator opens `Plan Compile` with either the returned durable `plan_compile_run_id` or a pending-launch projection tied to the approval command and idempotency key. If `PlanApproved` publication or projection reconciliation lags, the tab displays pending-launch status and then binds to the durable `PlanCompileRun` without creating a duplicate.

items.title: Launch controls are scoped and duplicate launch labels are forbidden
items.statement: The GUI cannot expose START, BUILD, or Approve & Continue for the same approval inputs; Open Build remains disabled until build identity exists and HITL continuation uses a scoped blocked action carrying approval scope, disabled reason, and receipt evidence.

evidence.exact_quote: The Orchestrator GUI must not expose `START`, `BUILD`, or `Approve & Continue` as ordinary launch controls for the same approval inputs. Retained controls use scoped commands: `Open Plan Compile` focuses the Plan Compile tab, `Open Build` is disabled until `BuildStarted` or a resulting build identity exists, and HITL continuation uses `cmd.runtime.approve` or another blocked-action command with approval scope, disabled reason, and receipt evidence. Stale `tiers` tab ids are compatibility/search aliases only; active route payloads use `tab_id = plan_compile`.

items.title: Blocked and HITL decisions must be reconstructable
items.statement: Blocked/HITL route records retain the listed identity, display, snapshot, severity, review, chat, result, package, safe-point, lane, attempt, and promotion fields so a decision can be reconstructed from page state.

evidence.exact_quote: Blocked and HITL routing records preserve `/blocking/HITL`, `/model/effort/persona/account`, `/target`, `/display`, `/snapshot`, field-shape, resolution_thread, `/severity/blocking`, `/review/corroboration`, `/chat`, `/result`, `/package`, `/fallback`, safe-point, lane, review, attempt, and promotion fields so blocked decisions remain reconstructable from the displayed page state.

items.title: Concern mutations carry action audit metadata
items.statement: Every concern action exposes resulting lineage/status, confirmation level, rationale requirement, allowed actor kinds, and reversibility for audit and display.

evidence.exact_quote: Concern actions expose audit_fields and action metadata: resulting_status_or_lineage, confirmation_level, rationale_required, allowed_actor_kinds, and reversibility are mandatory fields for action audit and display.

items.title: Canonical concern lifecycle and creation authority
items.statement: Concern lifecycle states are active, acknowledged, resolved, and dismissed. Runtime, package/seam overseers, corroboration outcome, and graph-patch logic may create canonical concerns; workers only nominate them.

evidence.exact_quote: Concern is a high-level first-class Orchestrator object. The lifecycle includes active, acknowledged, resolved, and dismissed; runtime, package overseer, seam overseer, corroboration outcome, and graph patch logic may create canonical concerns, while workers nominate concerns rather than minting canonical concern records directly.

items.title: Acknowledgement cannot substitute for blocker resolution
items.statement: Acknowledgement is a distinct, advisory-only state for seen or accepted non-blocking concerns; action-required blockers cannot be acknowledged in place of resolution.

evidence.exact_quote: Acknowledgement policy preserves acknowledged as distinct from resolved and dismissed; it is for advisory `/minor/non-blocking` concerns the user has explicitly seen or `/accepted`, and blockers that require action cannot be acknowledged in place of resolution.

items.title: Projection trust gates mutation
items.statement: Projection state is one of current, refreshing, stale, degraded, or unavailable. Mutation-capable projections carry observation and revalidation metadata, and stale/degraded/unavailable projections disable mutation until direct owner revalidation.

evidence.exact_quote: - Orchestrator surfaces use the projection states `current`, `refreshing`, `stale`, `degraded`, and `unavailable`.

- Freshness is buildable state: mutation-capable projections carry `projection_state`, `last_observed_at`, `source_event_ref`, and `revalidation_route`; `stale`, `degraded`, and `unavailable` disable mutation unless the owner surface performs current direct revalidation first.

items.title: Degraded projections fall back without closing the surface
items.statement: On trust loss, current projection surfaces remain open with freshness and degraded-state disclosure plus refresh/recovery, and fall back to record-backed History, Ledger, and direct evidence; only generation-matched current records support action.

evidence.exact_quote: Projection fallback prefers projection-backed current surfaces; when trust drops, the surface stays open with last-updated, degraded reason, refresh/recover action, and a fallback to `/record`, record-backed History, Ledger, and direct evidence inspectors.

Stale projection fallback degrades from summary `/projection` surfaces to direct record-backed inspection; Ledger and direct record views are the trust anchor under degraded projection health, and only current `/generation-matched` direct records may support action.

items.title: Search results are run-aware route payloads
items.statement: Search and command-palette results must preserve focused run, destination tab, selected object identity, optional filter and inspector detail, avoid name-based collapse across runs, and route using the shared record envelope.

evidence.exact_quote: Search results carry canonical route targets rather than highlight-only matches: focused_run_id, destination tab, selected object id, optional filter payload, optional inspector `/detail`, and detail target must be reconstructable from the result.

Search and command-palette routing remains `/object-first`: results preserve exact run identity, avoid collapsing similarly named seams, `/packages/nodes`, or work packages across unrelated runs, and use the shared record-envelope route payload rather than highlight-only matches.

items.title: Promotion gates and transitions remain decomposed
items.statement: Promotion visibility exposes lane-to-package, package-to-seam availability, seam completion, review/runtime/remediation/critical and GUI-readiness facts separately; promotion is explicit runtime state, automation-first, with optional HITL and multi-surface critical-state presentation.

evidence.exact_quote: Promotion-gate visibility is canonical Orchestrator data: lane_to_package, package_to_seam_available, seam_complete, package-level, package-overseer, `/review`, `/runtime`, `/remediation`, `/critical`, seam-consumable, and GUI readiness must be visible as separate gate facts rather than collapsed into a generic promotion state.

Promotion state transitions are explicit runtime state, not implicit side effects: automation-first remains the default, optional HITL may pause an otherwise-valid promotion, and `/HITL/critical` promotion states must surface on Dashboard, Orchestrator, and a spawned chat thread.

items.title: All affordances and mutations carry safety classification
items.statement: Every affordance is classified for navigation versus mutation, palette/shortcut exposure, multi-target safety, confirmation, and reversibility; bulk actions default to navigation and triage.

evidence.exact_quote: - Every affordance is classified by navigation vs mutation, palette visibility, shortcut eligibility, multi-target safety, and confirmation/reversibility.
- Bulk actions default to navigation and triage rather than live execution mutation.

items.title: Only Progress is widget-composed
items.statement: Widget composition is restricted to Progress, whose layout persists independently from Dashboard and Usage; other canonical tabs are native Orchestrator surfaces.

evidence.exact_quote: Native surface ownership preserves `Widget_System.md`, Widget_System, `Orchestrator_Page.md`, Orchestrator_Page, widget-composed, widget-heavy, and Progress compatibility: only Progress remains widget-heavy, while Plan Compile, Node Graph, Seams, Evidence, History, and Ledger are native Orchestrator surfaces.
- Widget-composed Orchestrator content is restricted to `Progress`.

items.title: Notifications propagate by severity, owner, persistence, and trust
items.statement: History receives chronological notification history, active operational surfaces receive warnings and blockers, decision channels are reserved for user decisions, advisory warnings may use quiet windows, and canonical blockers may not be quieted.

evidence.exact_quote: Notification mapping sends everything chronologically to History; Progress and Dashboard show active warnings, attention, blocked states, `/severity` markers, and badges; `/thread`, chat, or `/input` surfaces are reserved for user decisions, while system notifications stay high-value and sparse.
- Quiet windows are allowed for advisory warnings, but never for canonical blocked episodes.

items.title: Shared record envelope and family payload contract
items.statement: Governance/runtime records use a common envelope and structured family-specific payloads for concerns, promotions, recovery, and reviews; corroboration, promotion, graph-patch, and projection-trust payload/state/key/revalidation contracts are delegated to the CV-315/SP-233 owner pair.

evidence.exact_quote: Governance/runtime records use a shared record-envelope plus a family payload block. Concern payloads carry severity, category, owner, lifecycle, and resolution_kind; promotion payloads carry promotion_class, source_scope, target_scope, canonical verdict, and revoked `/reopened` lineage; recovery payloads carry blocked episode refs, action ids, preconditions, results, and safe-point refs; review payloads carry review scope, findings counts, unresolved findings, verdict, and canonical findings summary refs. Corroboration, promotion, graph-patch, and projection-trust records consume the `CV-315` / `SP-233` contract-storage owner pair for payload fields, state transitions, durable keys, and revalidation gates. Family payloads remain structured records distinct from artifacts or rendered summaries.

items.title: Project summary and attention projections have shared consumers
items.statement: Project summary exposes activity, attention, health, owner and projection trust with canonical blockers overriding weaker warnings; attention rows carry primary routes and trust disclosure and are shared by Orchestrator, Dashboard, and notifications.

evidence.exact_quote: - `project_summary` contains `activity_state`, `attention_state`, `health_state`, `owner`, and projection-trust disclosure.
- The same attention row is consumable across Orchestrator, Dashboard, and notifications.

items.title: Wait and timeout rendering follows owner truth
items.statement: Wait state is rendered from runtime/storage projections; absent fresh observations do not become failure until the owner reports a miss or threshold, known long waits do not trigger stall behavior, and actual expiry preserves a timeout class and routes recovery through a stored blocked episode or receipt.

evidence.exact_quote: - Orchestrator renders wait and timeout semantics from canonical runtime/storage projections rather than guessing from elapsed wall-clock time.

- When a timer actually expires, the visible card shows the retained `timeout_class` (`hard execution timeout`, `inactivity timeout`, `polling timeout`, `reconnect timeout`, or `user-visible wait timer expiry`) and routes recovery through the stored blocked episode or receipt.

items.title: External side-effect outcomes remain explicit and reconcilable
items.statement: External operation receipts expose missing links rather than omitting them, represent indeterminate remote outcomes and later reconciliation, preserve safe local capability during remote degradation, protect run-owned mutable targets, and apply informational terminal precedence to cancel/complete races.

evidence.exact_quote: - External side-effect receipts distinguish local-vs-remote and vs-remote outcomes. `indeterminate_remote_outcome` records `requested`, `transport_lost`, and later `reconciled` state plus a `Refresh remote state` CTA. Capability-level degradation and the local-vs-remote degraded-mode split keep local work available where safe: local Git can continue during hosted-degraded GitHub state, Docker local runtime can continue during registry outage, and manifest editing can continue while cluster access is offline.

- Terminal-state precedence rules for cancel/complete races are explicit; examples: cancel requested after a remote run already completed, container stop requested after the container already exited or restarted, and rollout cancel requested after a new revision already became ready. The receipt reconciles to an informational terminal state such as `completed_before_cancel`, `already_stopped`, or `already_replaced` instead of overwriting the completed outcome as failed.

items.title: Owner-surface command routing forbids panel-local mutation semantics
items.statement: Orchestrator owner-surface commands are route-open pivots preserving run/node/blocked-sequence/receipt context; runtime mutation recovery uses ordered runtime action ids, and Orchestrator cannot invent Source Control, Actions, Docker, Kubernetes, evidence, or artifact mutations.

evidence.exact_quote: Orchestrator UICommand exposure for recovery and navigation is delegated to `Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md`. Orchestrator may surface `cmd.orchestrator.open_in_source_control`, `cmd.orchestrator.open_in_github_actions`, `cmd.orchestrator.open_in_docker_manager`, `cmd.orchestrator.open_kubernetes`, and `cmd.orchestrator.open_receipt` only as route-open pivots into owner surfaces with the same `run_id`, `node_id?`, `blocked_sequence?`, `receipt_ref?`, and target owner context carried by the blocked episode or artifact receipt. Runtime mutation recovery still maps through ordered `allowed_action_ids[]` to `cmd.runtime.*`; Orchestrator MUST NOT mint panel-local mutation semantics for Source Control, GitHub Actions, Docker Manager, Kubernetes, evidence, or artifact actions.

items.title: Focused run remains stable across live and historical modes
items.statement: The page tracks active and focused run identifiers with explicit live/historical focus mode, and cross-tab links and search pivots stay on the focused run without silently returning to the active run.

evidence.exact_quote: - Orchestrator uses `active_run_id` / `focused_run_id` together with `focus_mode = live | historical`.
- Cross-tab deep links and search pivots stay coherent on the focused run rather than jumping back to the active run implicitly.

items.title: Debug resume revalidates all linked identities
items.statement: Before resuming Debug, Orchestrator revalidates dev, browser, DAP, and remote authority identities; recoverable staleness and absent nondeterministic targets become distinct attention-required reasons, and no replacement identity may be inferred.

evidence.exact_quote: - Before Orchestrator resumes a Debug investigation, it revalidates the linked `dev_session_id`, `browser_session_id`, DAP session identity, and remote authority against the stored route and runtime identity. If any linked identity is stale but recoverable, the run stays in `attention_required` with `attention_required_reason_code = session_reconnect_required`; if the linked identity no longer exists and no deterministic rebinding target exists, it stays in `attention_required` with `attention_required_reason_code = target_selection_required`. Orchestrator must not silently mint or infer a different target identity to continue execution.

items.title: Account pressure and switch events are append-only shared families
items.statement: Orchestrator stores append-only account pressure and account switch families consumed identically by Usage, History, Ledger, and Orchestrator.

evidence.exact_quote: - Orchestrator stores append-only `account_pressure_episode` and `account_switch_event` families.
- Usage, History, Ledger, and Orchestrator all consume the same durable event family.

items.title: Lane operations and concrete worktree operations have separate owners
items.statement: Orchestrator owns lane-pool operational truth while Source Control owns concrete repository/worktree operations; unified inventory includes assistant- and orch-owned worktrees and preserves available ownership and execution references.

evidence.exact_quote: Orchestrator remains the lane-pool operational truth, while Source Control is the concrete repo/worktree operator.

Source Control's unified worktree inventory includes assistant-owned worktrees alongside orch-owned worktrees. Rows preserve the owning thread, package, lane, run, and worktree refs available for each owner class, so this boundary is a shared ownership statement rather than exclusive orch ownership.

items.title: Blocked-owner labels conflict with the exact eight-kind taxonomy
items.statement: The window calls Run, Concern, Source Control, GitHub, Auth, Usage pressure, Wizard, and Recovery canonical blocked/attention owner examples, but later declares a different exact eight-kind blocked-owner taxonomy. It provides no mapping between these two sets, leaving serialization, filtering, and display normalization ambiguous.
items.impact: Builders can emit incompatible owner values and consumers cannot reliably aggregate or route blocked rows.
items.builder_discretion: A builder would have to invent whether the earlier names are reason/display labels, subtypes, aliases, or invalid owner kinds and define a mapping to the exact taxonomy.

evidence.exact_quote: Blocked-owner summaries identify the primary blocked owner or attention owner instead of only saying blocked; canonical examples include Run, Concern, Source Control, GitHub, Auth, Usage pressure, Wizard, and Recovery.
- Blocked-owner kinds are exactly `Runtime`, `Package Overseer`, `Seam Overseer`, `Corroboration`, `Graph Patch`, `Recovery`, `User`, and `External Resource`.

items.title: Concern action matrix is required but not instantiated
items.statement: The specification requires a matrix covering confirmation, rationale, performer, reversibility, and lineage for every action family, but the authoritative window provides no per-action rows or exhaustive binding from each named action to those values.
items.impact: Authorization and confirmation behavior can diverge across UI, runtime, and audit implementations.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must assign actor permissions, confirmation levels, reversibility, rationale requirements, and lineage effects for each action.

evidence.exact_quote: The canonical concern action matrix spans confirmation level, rationale requirements, who may perform the action, reversibility model, and lineage side effects for every action family.

items.title: Projection freshness naming and transition authority remain explicitly open
items.statement: Projection-freshness naming/ownership and concern-transition authority splits are declared design-open until other owners close them, so this window cannot supply a final ownership or authority contract.
items.impact: A builder cannot finalize the owner of freshness state or the definitive transition authorization checks from this document alone.
items.builder_discretion: No local discretion should close the question; implementation must defer to the owning contract once adjudicated.

evidence.exact_quote: Open owner-decision guardrails remain explicit rather than hidden: requested concrete account, operational identity / actor role, switch-history and pressure timeline, projection-freshness naming/ownership, and concern-transition authority splits retain design-open status until their owning docs close them. Usage and account projections stay project-scoped by default; multi-project aggregation is a separate later concern, and per-project Orchestrator storage `/projection` remains the active direction.

items.title: Concrete account and cross-document identity ownership remain open
items.statement: Requested concrete account, switch history, conversational actor fields, and trust behavior cross ownership boundaries and are explicitly not closed in this window.
items.impact: Account identity, pressure history, and trust projections may be duplicated or inconsistently owned.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must not invent a final owner or collapse account identity and actor-role semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: Cross-doc account ownership remains open for `Multi-Account.md` references: design-open questions are not closed while requested concrete account, switch history, conversational actor fields, and trust behavior still cross-doc ownership boundaries.

items.title: Concern update heuristics lack deterministic merge and mint rules
items.statement: Repeated sightings are said to use source/scope/category/lineage-aware heuristics, but no precedence, identity key, time window, or conflict rule defines when to update versus mint.
items.impact: Equivalent event streams can produce different concern counts, identities, and histories.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent matching weights, keys, thresholds, and tie-breaking behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: - Repeated sightings use source/scope/category/lineage-aware heuristics to decide whether to update an existing concern or mint a new concern record.

items.title: Scale mechanisms have no measurable performance oracle
items.statement: Virtualization and demand-loading are mandatory across dense tabs, but the window defines no dataset sizes, latency targets, memory budgets, frame-rate thresholds, pagination limits, or degraded behavior to prove compliance.
items.impact: Implementations can claim compliance while exhibiting materially different usability and resource costs.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose all scale thresholds and measurement conditions.

evidence.exact_quote: - Slice-based loading, virtualization, lazy expansion, and demand-loaded inspectors are mandatory across dense tabs.
- Scale is a cross-tab contract rather than a graph-tab-only concern.

items.title: Pending Plan Compile reconciliation has no failure or expiry contract
items.statement: The happy path binds a pending launch to a durable PlanCompileRun, but the window gives no timeout, terminal failure state, retry/reconcile command, or user recovery behavior when publication or reconciliation never succeeds.
items.impact: The tab can remain indefinitely pending or risk unsafe manual retry behavior despite the no-duplicate requirement.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose expiry, retry, error display, receipt inspection, and idempotent reconciliation behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: Orchestrator Plan Compile consumes the Planning Wizard `Approve And Build` approval transaction; it does not create a second ordinary build launch. When `cmd.planning_wizard.approve_and_build` succeeds locally, Orchestrator opens `Plan Compile` with either the returned durable `plan_compile_run_id` or a pending-launch projection tied to the approval command and idempotency key. If `PlanApproved` publication or projection reconciliation lags, the tab displays pending-launch status and then binds to the durable `PlanCompileRun` without creating a duplicate.

items.title: Security and privacy handling for retained identity snapshots is unspecified
items.statement: Blocked routes preserve model, persona, account, display, snapshot, chat, result, and review context, but this window defines no data classification, redaction, retention, visibility boundary, encryption, or least-privilege read policy for those fields.
items.impact: Sensitive account, conversation, review, and result context may be over-retained or exposed to unauthorized actors and surfaces.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must determine what is sensitive, who can read it, how it is redacted, and how long it persists.

evidence.exact_quote: Blocked and HITL routing records preserve `/blocking/HITL`, `/model/effort/persona/account`, `/target`, `/display`, `/snapshot`, field-shape, resolution_thread, `/severity/blocking`, `/review/corroboration`, `/chat`, `/result`, `/package`, `/fallback`, safe-point, lane, review, attempt, and promotion fields so blocked decisions remain reconstructable from the displayed page state.

items.title: Legacy compatibility has no migration or retirement oracle
items.statement: Tier-era routes, keys, APIs, branch naming, and tab labels are retained as compatibility fields, but the window provides no translation versioning, conflict precedence, telemetry, deprecation schedule, or removal acceptance criteria.
items.impact: Legacy aliases can remain execution-significant accidentally or diverge from node/package/seam/lane identity indefinitely.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose alias translation, collision handling, warning behavior, and retirement criteria.

evidence.exact_quote: Worktree legacy compatibility is explicit: `WorktreeGitImprovement.md`, `/tier`, `/node`, tier_id, `/storage`, `/package`, `/worktree`, get_tier_worktree, get_tier_worktree(tier_id), owner run/tier, tier-keyed, tier-based branch/worktree naming, and older `Progress, Tiers, History, and Node Graph` labels are retained as compatibility fields, not execution-canonical authority over lane/package/node attempts. The active shell remains `Progress`, `Plan Compile`, `Seams`, `Node Graph`, `Evidence`, `History`, and `Ledger`.

items.title: Escalation vocabularies lack an explicit cross-taxonomy mapping
items.statement: The window names Info/Warning/Attention/Action Required alert levels, advisory/attention_required/blocked/escalated/degraded_projection widget alerts, and info/watch/attention_required/blocked/escalated escalation levels, but does not state whether these are separate layers or how values map across surfaces.
items.impact: Dashboard, Orchestrator, widgets, thread badges, and notifications can show inconsistent severity for the same underlying record.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent normalization and surface-specific mapping among the three vocabularies.

evidence.exact_quote: Alert levels separate Info, Warning, Attention, and Action Required; Dashboard summarizes `/urgency`, Orchestrator provides operational alert context, and a chat thread is reserved for situations that need user `/decision` rather than general warnings.
- Escalation levels are `info`, `watch`, `attention_required`, `blocked`, and `escalated`, with surface mapping across Orchestrator banners, Dashboard summaries, thread badges, and notifications.

items.title: Persistent blocker resurfacing trigger is not operationally defined
items.statement: Persistent blockers must resurface on meaningful change or persistence, but neither meaningful change nor persistence duration, deduplication, backoff, or quiet-period reset is defined.
items.impact: Implementations may spam users or fail to resurface long-lived blockers.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must select timing thresholds, change detection, cadence, and notification deduplication.

evidence.exact_quote: - `attention_required` remains distinct from `blocked`, and persistent blockers resurface on meaningful change or persistence.

items.title: Help architecture lacks the required entry schema and linkage behavior
items.statement: The window requires a dedicated help-entry architecture with related-concept linking, but does not define entry fields, identifier stability, search/index behavior, localization, ownership, or broken-link validation.
items.impact: Help entries and related-concept clusters cannot be implemented or tested consistently.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must define the help data model and all navigation, search, and validation behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: - Help uses a dedicated help-entry architecture with related-concept linking.

dimension_assessments.summary: Launch, action, wait, routing, acknowledgement, escalation, focus, and fallback behaviors are explicit, with bounded gaps in recovery and timing.
The window specifies scheduling/concern/runtime identity, search, projection, widget, web-evidence, external pivot, history, and recovery capabilities.
Commands, route identities, record envelopes, family payloads, projection fields, event families, and cross-surface outputs are named.
Many record and routing contracts are explicit, but the per-action authority matrix and deterministic concern identity/update contract are absent.
Concern, projection, promotion, wait, focused-run, external outcome, and debug-attention states are explicit; concern-transition authority remains open.
Page/runtime/storage/scheduler and owner-surface boundaries are explicit, but the action matrix, concern transition split, and blocked-owner normalization remain unresolved.
Orchestrator, Source Control, runtime/storage/scheduler, Usage, and shared contract owners are distinguished; account and freshness ownership remain explicitly open.
Dashboard, Progress, History, Ledger, Usage, notifications, chat, owner panels, and shared projection consumers are explicitly routed.
Tab shell, scoped controls, native/widget boundaries, projection trust presentation, and route behavior are explicit, but help architecture and alert normalization remain underspecified.
Projection fallback, timeout classes, external indeterminacy, cancel races, blocked pivots, and debug revalidation are specified; pending Plan Compile lacks a terminal recovery path.

Actor authority, confirmation, mutation gating, and run-owned target protection provide safety controls, but sensitive retained routing and identity data has no confidentiality, redaction, retention, or visibility contract.
The same concern, attention, account, receipt, promotion, escalation, and blocked state is propagated to named consumers with trust and route context.
Receipts, reconciliation, revalidation, blocked pivots, external degradation, focus, and Source Control handoff are operationally described, with open timing and pending-launch recovery decisions.
Cross-tab slice loading, virtualization, lazy expansion, and demand-loaded inspectors are mandatory, but there are no measurable budgets or acceptance thresholds.
Tier-era compatibility aliases are explicitly noncanonical, but translation, deprecation, collision handling, and retirement criteria are absent.

Exact tab, lifecycle, projection, timeout, command, escalation, and blocked-owner tokens provide partial oracles; performance, taxonomy mapping, help, action-matrix, and pending-launch recovery oracles are missing.

Consequential discretion remains for owner taxonomy normalization, action permissions, open ownership decisions, concern identity, performance budgets, recovery, privacy, migration, escalation mapping, resurfacing, and help architecture.
The review found explicit open owner decisions plus conflicting owner labels and unmapped alert vocabularies; these cannot be safely inferred from the assigned window.
